newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher on technicals and NAPM.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher on technicals and NAPM.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended at a three-week high Thursday after a breach of resistance and against the backdrop of a stronger-than-expected December NAPM index, traders said.
March copper ended up 1.90 cents at 102.15 cents a lb after breaching resistance at 101.20, the highest level seen in December.

"The breach of the 101.20 level in March copper triggered some stop orders, which looked to be fresh fund buying, rather than short covering," Deutsche Sharps Pixley trader Richard Hirsch said. "In addition, the jump in the December NAPM index suggested demand was going to stay strong, while overall exchange stocks remain low."
The December National Association of Purchasing Managers Index rose to 54.0 from 52.7 in November. A reading above 50 pct indicates an expansion in the manufacturing sector.
The COMEX January/March spread held steady around 2.45 cents.
Earlier, LME three-month copper had tested resistance around $2170 a tonne, although a further recovery in LME warehouse copper stocks from six-year lows is expected in Friday's data.
In the past month, both COMEX and LME copper had been drifting back from six-month highs as LME stocks recovered from six-year lows.
But Chinese demand, combined with normal growth in the rest of the world, is likely to consume almost all of the extra copper coming on stream in 1997, analysts said.
